@adamgrant is an organizational psychologist, bestselling author and professor at the Wharton School of the University of Pennsylvania. He is widely known for studying how people think, work, collaborate and build relationships. His research explores what motivates people, how teams function, why some individuals succeed while others struggle, and how workplaces can become more productive and fulfilling. Through his work, he challenges conventional ideas about success, leadership and human behaviour.

Adam is the author of several bestselling books, including Give and Take, Originals, Option B (co-authored with Sheryl Sandberg), Think Again and Hidden Potential. His books explore topics such as generosity, creativity, rethinking beliefs, overcoming setbacks and developing human potential. His work combines psychological research with practical insights that people can apply to their careers, relationships and everyday decisions. He is also known for his TED Talks, podcast Rethinking and ability to make complex psychological concepts accessible to a broad audience.

In his work, Adam focuses on helping people become better thinkers, colleagues, leaders and friends. He examines how to recognise genuine generosity, challenge assumptions, give and receive feedback, and build stronger connections with others. His book Vibe explores the dynamics of relationships and how people connect with one another. By bringing together research and real-world examples, Adam encourages people to rethink how they approach work, friendships and personal growth.

In Today’s Episode, He Talks About How to Vibe With People and Build Connection

At 21, I was making around £3,000 a month in profit while studying medicine full-time.

I’d combined three things I was already good at: teaching, building websites and the BMAT medical-school entrance exam.

So I created a course to help other students prepare for it.

For the first few years, I did almost everything myself.

Then one weekend, I couldn’t teach, so I asked if my two friends wanted to run the course without me and get paid for it. Of course they said yes. 

The feedback was just as good as it was when it was just me running it. 

That was a huge unlock for me when I realised the business didn’t need me to deliver every part of it.

Delegating helped me scale my time, but I also accidentally outsourced the part I enjoyed most.

So, two lessons:

1️⃣ You don’t need to do everything yourself.

2️⃣ Be careful not to delegate the work you actually love.

After all, what’s the point of running a business if you’re not having fun?

Follow @aliabdaal for more stories like this :)

The best way to make university useful for your career isn’t always getting perfect grades.

First, work out how much your grades actually matter. If a first-class degree or 4.0 GPA will meaningfully improve your career prospects, then obviously it’s worth optimising for them.

But for many careers, employers stop caring about your grades fairly quickly.

So, use some of your spare time to go on side quests and build valuable skills. Learn to code, edit videos, design websites, write, sell or use AI tools.

Your degree might help you get your first job, but the skills you build alongside it could shape the rest of your career. 

And if you want to know what skills you have that could become a business idea, comment CRAFT and I’ll send you my custom GPT that will interview you and help figure out what your craft skills are 👇
Advice to my younger self 😌

When I was 18, I got scammed out of £1,000.

At the time, that was literally all the money I had. I’d spent two years tutoring maths for £15 an hour to save for a MacBook Air, only to discover I’d paid £1,000 for an old laptop worth about £200.

It was painful. But I decided I was going to make the money back, and then make 10 times more.

That decision prompted me to start my first proper business.

Over the next few years, it generated more than £1 million in revenue. I eventually sold it and used the money to start another business, which has since generated over £10 million.

Obviously, I wouldn’t recommend getting scammed.

But sometimes the worst moments can become surprisingly useful fuel for whatever you do next.

Comment FOUNDATIONS if you want to build your own $100k a year lifestyle business - to get access to my free 7-lesson course from @lifestylebusinessacademy 👇

I used to assume that a successful business should keep growing: more revenue, more people, more complexity.

But there’s a difficult middle ground between a small lifestyle business and a larger performance business.

Once the team grows beyond roughly 12 people, you often need proper management layers and a completely different way of operating.

Every time we’ve reached 15–18 people, things have started to break, and we’ve ended up returning to a smaller core team.

Right now, that’s what I want.

I’ve got a kid, we’ve recently moved to Hong Kong, and I want more space for family, health and life outside work.

Maybe one day I’ll want to build a huge company. But for now, I’m choosing fun, freedom and flexibility.

Because bigger isn’t automatically better. It depends on the life you’re trying to build.

If I were starting a business today with no audience, I’d keep it simple.

I’d choose a skill I already have like content creation, marketing or AI automation and offer it as a service to someone in my existing network.

At first, I’d charge a discounted rate and offer a strong guarantee. The goal wouldn’t be to maximise profit.

It would be to get a great result, testimonial and case study.

Then I’d use that proof to find more clients.

Over time, I’d hire someone, productise the service and potentially turn it into a product. Alongside that, I’d build a personal brand around the skill.

You don’t need an audience or a perfectly scalable idea to begin, so don’t let that hold you back.

Start by solving one real problem for one real person and build from there.

Comment FOUNDATIONS for my free 7-lesson course on how to build a $100k a year business if I were starting again with a full-time job 👇

I made my first £30 online when I was 12.

I’d decided to learn website design, so I emailed everyone I knew asking if they needed a website. One person said yes, and only then did I figure out the HTML and CSS. 

I had no degree, no experience and, frankly, very little idea what I was doing. I just found someone with a problem, offered to solve it and learned the skills along the way.

That £30 completely changed how I thought about work. I realised I could get paid to learn something I’d happily have done for free.

And honestly, that’s still some of my favourite advice for new entrepreneurs: don’t wait until you feel qualified. Find a real problem, offer to solve it, and work out the details as you go.

I read this book 10 years ago when I first started investing back in 2015 and it taught me everything you need to know about investing. posts.caption: Everybody is jealous of the destination. Nobody is jealous of the journey.

5 money rules my wife and I follow as a couple aged 45 with two kids.

1. We don’t spend money to look rich. 

We spend to become wealthy and gain freedom of our time.

So, there’s no car. It’s rented. 
We own the house we live in, no other real estate.

No spending on brands. No spending just to show off to people.

2. We spend extravagantly on high-quality food.

We know that what goes into our body is ultimately the biggest wealth we have, and unfortunately, healthy food is not cheap.

3. We spend on experiences more than things.

Things give you happiness once, and they have no end.

You remember experiences, and they make you a better person. 
You grow as a person.

We travelled 116 days last year!

4. We invest before spending.

As soon as our salary comes, the largest amount is invested.

The remaining amount is used for expenses.

We are recording this on the 30th. 
₹9,000 and ₹600 left in our bank accounts. 
Everything else is invested.

5. No budget for books and learning.

No amount of money spent is enough.

Ruchi is learning pottery, watercolor painting, and tennis.

Our kids also go to many classes.

These are our rules. 
They may not apply to you, but having your own rules is important in life.

Before you say yes to marriage, check these 5 things.

1. Why are you getting married? Is it for the sake of society? Is it for the sake of your parents? Is it for your own good?

2. How do you handle fights with your partner? Because fights will continue. If you handle them properly, then relationships will progress.

3. Do you have an alignment on money and responsibility? How will you spend money? How will you share responsibilities?

4. Do you have space for your own personality? You can make friends without involving their friends. You can live your own life without depending on them.

5. How will you spend your life after marriage? What are the expectations from your family? How will your daily routines be? What will be your living arrangements? What have you thought about your children?

This is an important decision. Don't take it in a hurry.

5 signs that a friendship might be coming to an end.

1/ You find out what's happening in their life through Instagram stories.

2/ Your conversations have become occasional birthday, New Year and festival wishes.

3/ You rehearse every message before sending it because you're afraid of how they'll react.

4/ When something big happens in your life, they're no longer among the first people you want to tell.

5/ You know the friendship is over, but you're waiting for them to end it.

Not every friendship needs to last a lifetime. 
Sometimes, letting go is more important than holding on.

There’s a hidden cost to caring too much about what people think.

Slowly, you stop living your life and start performing it. 
The choices become theirs. 
The approval becomes the goal.

And one day you realise you built a whole life around people whose opinions you’ll barely remember in ten years.

Their approval was never the prize.

Your own life was.

3 approaches we use to solve our fights.

1/ Fight in private. 
Never disagree in front of other people or the kids.

2/ Don’t sleep over a fight. 
If we’ve had a fight, we resolve it before going to sleep.

3/ Fight the problem, not each other. 
We don’t focus on who is right or wrong. 
We focus on solving the problem.

A healthy relationship isn’t one without fights.

It’s one where you know how to handle them.

We confuse intensity with love all the time.

The obsession, the jealousy, the way they seem flawless, the way we lose ourselves in them. 
It feels like love. 
Often it’s just a crush wearing love’s clothes.

Real love is calmer than that. 
It sees the faults, makes room for a life outside each other, and never asks you to disappear.

Tag the person you’d happily fail all three of these for.

The best time to change your job might be when you're performing at your best - not when you're desperate to leave.

Don't wait until your manager treats you badly, your appraisal goes wrong, or your workplace becomes toxic.

When your work is valued, you're delivering results, and your skills are in demand, you have more leverage to explore better opportunities.

Make your next career move from a position of strength, not weakness.

In the beginning, money feels like it’s for proving something.

The gadget, the brand, the upgrade that shows you’ve arrived.

But the two things that actually pay you back are something different. 

1/ Spending on your own skills, because that’s what raises everything you’ll ever earn. 

2/ And spending on your parents, because that window doesn’t stay open forever.

Skill yourself. 
Take care of them.

Everything else can wait.

linkedin.about:
I’m the founder and CEO of Thrive Global, a behavior change technology company with the mission of improving health and helping us move from merely surviving to thriving. I also founded The Huffington Post and have written 15 books, including Thrive and The Sleep Revolution.

I’m originally from Greece (and still have the accent to prove it!). When I was 17, I moved to England and studied economics at Cambridge University, where I frankly spent most of my time debating at the Cambridge Union.

I live in New York but also spend time in Los Angeles, and love being a Yiayia (Greek for grandmother) to my almost three-year-old grandson Alexander and his newborn sister Annabel.

My journey to focusing on health began with a fall. In April 2007, I collapsed from exhaustion and burnout and hit my head on my desk on the way down, breaking my cheekbone.
 
In the wake of my fall, I found myself going from doctor to doctor to find out what was wrong. Doctors’ waiting rooms were good places for me to ask myself a lot of questions about the kind of life I was living.

After all the tests, it turned out nothing was wrong. Except for the fact that everything was wrong. I was suffering from an acute case of burnout. I had bought into the myth that burnout was the price I had to pay for success. 

I became more and more passionate about the five daily habits that drive so much of our health: nutrition, exercise, sleep, stress management and connection. That led me to write Thrive and The Sleep Revolution. 

The books struck a chord, but I wanted to go beyond speaking and writing to helping people move from awareness to action. So in 2016 I founded Thrive Global, which helps people transform their health by combining Microsteps — small, science-backed daily steps — with technology, storytelling and community. And last year, with the OpenAI Startup Fund, we launched Thrive AI Health to build an AI health coach to democratize access to health coaching.

posts.caption:
I love technology. I’ve started two very tech-centric companies. But ultimately, technology is just a tool, one that can add to our lives or deplete and diminish them. Much like a hammer: a very useful tool, but not if you hit yourself in the head with it, which produces roughly the same cognitive effect as doomscrolling.

The good news is that more and more people are choosing to put the hammer down.

“Bloomscrolling” is a growing trend of choosing uplifting, inspiring content over the endless doomscroll. And it matters. @Harvard experts link heavy consumption of distressing news to anxiety, depression, headaches, poor sleep, low appetite and higher blood pressure.

People are acting on this beyond the feed, too. @Pinterest reports searches for “offline hobbies” are up 551% year over year, and searches for “no phone ideas” are climbing as well.

The grab for our attention is the new gold rush, and our attention is our most precious resource. That’s why I believe no one should have phones on the table during a meal. There are few things better than sharing a meal with a friend without being constantly tempted to check your phone.

So today, try one Microstep: before you close your feed, follow one account that leaves you feeling inspired, and unfollow one that leaves you feeling depleted.

Read more in @FastCompany at the link in bio.

posts.caption:
What a remarkable day at #ThinkHealth, Alice Walton’s health and AI conference at the @heartlandwholehealthinstitute in Bentonville.

Every time I’m in Bentonville, I’m more inspired by what Alice is building. First came the @crystalbridgesmuseum. Then the Heartland Whole Health Institute and the @awsom_med. And next up is the AWSOM Whole Health Campus. It’s another step toward bringing to life Alice’s vision of integrating health, art and nature.

It was the perfect setting to share my interview with Daniela Amodei, president of Anthropic. With everyone at the company reporting to her, Daniela is not only a key AI leader, but the most prominent woman leader at a time when the AI conversation is dominated by men. She’s at the forefront of frontier models, but she also studied literature, she played the flute, she’s a mother. She doesn’t just speak tech, she speaks about nature, community, friendship and self-reflection.

We spoke about the need to expand the public conversation to include not just recursive self-improvement for machines but recursive self-improvement for humans. Because the biggest risk for humanity is continuing to place all our bets on the machines. 

As Daniela put it, “The whole reason we’re developing this technology is to help humans flourish and thrive and live better lives.” We explored the potential for AI hyper-personalization to transform health and the value of wisdom in a world where AI is dethroning intelligence.

These themes carried through the rest of the day. I hosted a panel on AI, health and the future of brain resilience with @jenoleksiw, Group Vice President of US Neuroscience at @elilillyco; Tina Stankovic, professor and chair of head and neck surgery at @stanford.med; and @danielnadlerworkshop, Founder and CEO of @open.evidence. And I sat down with Nate Gross, who leads health at @openai and has been called “a human encyclopedia of digital health.”

Thank you, Alice, for bringing us all together for these vital conversations, and for all the work you’re doing to redefine the future of healthcare, both for the heartland and beyond.

In their beautiful new children’s book, Ocean of Stars, author Azita Ardakani and artist Rebecca Rebouché invite readers of every age to rediscover wonder and our connection to the world around us.

In a moment when answers are instant, Azita asks whether our capacity to be astonished is keeping up. She points to the stars and reminds us that the carbon in our bodies was forged in them. As she writes, “We are not simply living in the universe. We are an expression of it.”

posts.caption:
@OpenAI solved a problem mathematicians have wrestled with for a quarter century.

@GoogleDeepMind mapped every possible mutation hiding in our genes. These are awe-inspiring feats of the machines.

In my latest piece for @time, I write about why, even as we marvel at AI’s capacity, we shouldn’t lose sight of something irreplaceable: human-generated awe.

Dacher Keltner, professor of psychology at the @ucberkeleyofficial, looked at 2,600 stories of awe across 26 countries. He found that what most commonly led people to feel awe wasn’t nature, or spirituality, or technology — it was watching other people be kind, brave, or strong.

He calls it "moral beauty" and 95% of it comes from witnessing actions people take on behalf of others. Collective movement. Nature. Music. Visual design. Spirituality. Big ideas. Life and death. These are the other wonders Keltner found that inspire awe — and they’re all deeply shaped by human connection.

AI will keep astonishing us. But the awe that has the most profound impact is the awe we derive from each other. And as Keltner writes, that awe is available to us "if we just take a moment and wonder."

You can read my full piece at the link in bio.

posts.caption:
Today is World Mental Health Day. And we’ve made great progress in recent years raising awareness and opening up the conversation about mental health.

This year, I hope we take it one step further: mental health is brain health. A growing body of research shows how our brain health connects to everything from daily brain fog and anxiety to long-term cognitive decline.

So here’s a Microstep to try today: take a moment to check-in with your own mental health by naming the feeling you’re having right now in one word. Simply putting a feeling into words can help calm the brain’s stress response.

It might be “overwhelmed.” Or “tired.” Or “uncertain.”

Whatever it is, naming it is a small way to build the muscle of self-awareness, one of the most powerful tools we have for our mental and brain health.

posts.caption:
Right now, 75% of Americans are anxious and afraid about AI. People are even bringing their concerns into their therapy sessions, sorting through everything from how AI impacts their jobs to more existential fears about humanity’s future.

These concerns are real. But they’re only part of the story.

To go deeper, I sat down with Daniela Amodei. As president of Anthropic, she is a unique figure in AI. With everyone at the company reporting to her, she is not only a key AI leader, but the most prominent woman leader at a time when the AI conversation is dominated by men. She’s at the forefront of frontier models, but she also studied literature, she played the flute, she’s a mother. She doesn’t just speak tech, she speaks about nature, community, friendship, and self-reflection.

In my conversation with Daniela, we explore:
• why the discussion about recursive self-improvement has to include humans, not just the machines 
• the dance between humans and AI, and what happens when one partner keeps growing and the other stagnates
• letting AI own intelligence and letting humans own wisdom, and why “Claude can never be your manager, or your therapist, or your partner, or your kids”
• how AI’s power of hyper-personalization can transform health, because health is also about what happens between doctor visits when we improve our daily habits around food, movement, sleep, stress management and connection
• whether AI, unlike social media, can nurture our better angels instead of activating our lesser ones and strengthening the worst in us

Also:
• why her 5-year-old thinks her job is taking care of an alligator named Claude
• why Leaves of Grass and Yesteryear are both on her nightstand
• why there should never be an AI czar

Watch my full conversation with Daniela on my YouTube channel. Link in bio.

This is one of my favorite @thecuriosityshop episodes. In a world where everyone and everything is fighting for our attention, our rage, and our money, we exam what makes us vulnerable to persuasion and how we can develop stronger influence literacy skills.

Shame around being persuadable makes us more vulnerable to influence. Acknowledging that we are vulnerable to those reels and TikTok’s and snake oil pitches makes us more resistant!

posts.caption:
@adamgrant and I loved talking with @angelalduckworth about her new book, “Situated.”

Big takeaway:

“To stay motivated through the countless hours of practice that separate amateurs from experts, grit is necessary but not sufficient. The situation also matters—and to an astonishing degree:

Culture matters.
Mentors matter.
Teammates matter.
Even the objects in your personal space matter.

How you think about your goals and what you’re willing to do to achieve them depends on both you and your situation.”

I also loved our conversation about billboards - those signs we post around our spaces as reminders of what’s important. It reminds of why I like to write in a room where my children’s art is hanging. The kids’ art is my favorite art and it’s imperfect and honest. Grit is great, but I also need the environment to say, “Have fun. Just start.”

posts.caption:
When we see people attack empathy or say things like, “The fundamental weakness of Western civilization is empathy” (Elon Musk, 2025), we should ask ourselves, “What harm, pain, or hurt do they not want us to see or feel? Who do they want to hurt, humiliate, or dehumanize without accountability?”

Based on our research over the past 25 years, creating meaningful connections and human-centered systems requires a combination of compassion and cognitive empathy. I think of compassion as the daily practice and cognitive empathy as one its most powerful tools.

We define compassion as the daily practice of recognizing and accepting our shared humanity so that we treat ourselves and others with loving-kindness, and we take action in the face of suffering.

Most definitions of compassion share a commitment to action. It’s not just feeling, it’s doing. Compassion is fueled by accepting that we’re all made of strength and struggle—no one is immune to pain or suffering. Compassion is not a practice of “better than” or “I can fix you”—it’s a practice based in the beauty and pain of shared humanity.

Most researchers agree there are at least two elements to empathy: cognitive empathy and affective empathy. Cognitive empathy, sometimes called perspective taking, is the ability to recognize and understand another person’s emotions. Affective empathy, often called experience sharing, is one’s own emotional attunement with another person’s experience.

The empathy we desperately need is understanding what someone is feeling, not feeling it for them. If someone feels lonely, empathy doesn’t require us to feel lonely too, only to reach back into our own experience with loneliness so we can understand and connect. Affective empathy, feeling something along with the person who is struggling, is a slippery slope toward becoming too overwhelmed to offer meaningful support.

Again, empathy is a tool of compassion. We can respond empathically only if we are willing to be present to someone’s pain. If we’re not willing to do that, it’s not real empathy. And the lack of real empathy is 100% a major threat to civilizations.

Thank you to @toninovvva for this powerful reminder.
posts.alt:
We always say, “Imagine if it was your daughter, your sister, or your mother.” But you know what? Imagine having empathy and not needing to be personally affected to care. -Toninovvva 
On a cream background, black text, with purple highlighter.

experience.company: Author of Key Person of Influence | Entrepreneur Revolution | Oversubscribed | 24 Assets
experience.description:
In any given industry, some people struggle to get enough customers, while others have more than they can handle. Similarly, in any given market, some companies chase for clients, while others select who they want to work with and turn away the rest. What sets the latter groups apart?

In January 2013, I e-mailed clients in Sydney, Australia, saying, “We have sold too many tickets for the event that you’ve booked for. The venue holds 700 people, and we’re now forming a waiting list. If you’d like to sell your ticket back to us, we’ll pay you DOUBLE what you paid for it.” This wasn’t a joke, gimmick, or ploy. We had a similar problem in Melbourne 2 weeks later. 

The interesting thing was our event was brand new and was priced at the top end of the market. We didn’t have a single member of staff on the ground. So how did we achieve this when long-established businesses in the city couldn’t get 100 people to their events?

In this book I share the principles and method for becoming oversubscribed because I believe they improve business for everyone involved. When your business is oversubscribed, you do your best work, your clients receive the best service, and you have more downtime to innovate new products instead of running around continually selling old ones. 

This book is not just about marketing principles and business methods. It addresses some of the problems most businesses suffer from, and is written for quality businesses that care about what they do, and are passionate about it and the value it presents to the world. It is for people who want to genuinely serve their clients.

Purchase here on Amazon

experience.title: My Book: Entrepreneur Revolution
experience.company: Author of Key Person of Influence | Entrepreneur Revolution | Oversubscribed | 24 Assets
experience.description:
The idea of the entrepreneur revolution is that the rules that created commercial success in the past have changed radically. Doing what worked yesterday may not bring you success tomorrow. For some people, this is a time of great uncertainty and loss. For others, it is the greatest opportunity in history. 

I wrote this book to help individuals become better at spotting opportunities and making them successful and even better at spotting opportunities that are right for them. 

In the book I share the ‘entrepreneurial sweet spot’, where you get to do what you love, do it well, and be rewarded generously for it. It provides a way of creating a high-performance culture so that no matter how many complex decisions you face, you will always continue to move forward.  

A revolution is a great shift in society where an old system is thrown out and a new one is embraced. In all of history, real fortunes are made in revolutionary times. The difference with the current revolution is the chance it presents to spread the wealth of a lot more people. Right now your ideas have the potential to be massive, more than ever before in history.

Purchase here on Amazon

experience.title: My Book: Key Person of Influence
experience.company: Author of Key Person of Influence | Entrepreneur Revolution | Oversubscribed | 24 Assets
experience.description:
At the centre of every industry you will find an inner circle of people who are the most well known and valued. They are the ‘key people of influence’, or the KPI, as we call them. You probably already know these people in your industry:

Their names come up in conversations
…for all the right reasons.

They attract a lot of opportunities 
…the right sort.

They earn a lot more money than most people
… and it isn’t a struggle.

They can make a project successful if they are involved
… and people know it.

In 2006, when I arrived in the UK with nothing but a suitcase and a credit card, I didn’t know anyone. I was told it was almost impossible to crack into the Establishment and to network above my station, but I proved them wrong.

Within three years, people started calling me one of the most connected entrepreneurs in London. I had built a business turning over millions, and I could contact all of the high flyers and heavy hitters in my industry in just a few phone calls. 

Over the years with Triumphant Events, many people approached me wanting to speak on my stage, and it was then I noticed exactly what it was that made some people stand out and others not. I translated this learning into this book, which has gone on to be an international best-seller.

posts.caption:
Two women. Two of the biggest jobs in sports media. And absolutely no waiting on the sidelines of their own careers!! This week on Aspire, I’m sitting down with @taylorrooks, host of NBA on Prime and Thursday Night Football, and @malika_andrews, Emmy-winning journalist and host of ESPN’s NBA coverage.

Between them, they’re speaking to millions of people every week and interviewing some of the biggest athletes in the world. All in an industry that was built for men!!

But what I really wanted to understand was what it took to get there. Because getting the opportunity is one thing. Earning the trust, building the reputation and proving you deserve to stay there is something else entirely.

And the more successful you become, the more people have an opinion about who you are, what you’re worth and how you should do your job. I know a thing or two about that!!

We get into:
✨ Why preparation is the foundation of real confidence
✨ How to earn trust and credibility when the stakes are high
✨ Why you have to ask for what you want instead of waiting to be chosen
✨ How to negotiate for what you’re worth without letting others define your value
✨ Why building a lasting career matters more than chasing the next big opportunity

This conversation goes SO far beyond sports. Whether you’re building a business, climbing the corporate ladder or figuring out your next move, there’s so much to learn from how these two women have backed themselves and built careers on their own terms.

Our episode is out now on @youtube, @applepodcasts, @spotify and wherever you listen!! 🎙️
posts.alt: Video by Emma Grede on October 13, 2026. May be an image of one or more people, people standing, magazine, poster and text.

posts.caption:
I’ve never been someone who shies away from a difficult conversation. Anyone who knows me knows I’m pretty comfortable saying exactly what I think!!! 
But there’s a BIG difference between being willing to have a difficult conversation and knowing how to have one well. And that’s exactly why I wanted to sit down with this week’s guest on Aspire, @priyaparker!!

Priya has spent more than 20 years studying conflict, and her argument is that most of us don’t actually need LESS conflict in our lives. We need to learn how to do it BETTER. 

We spend so much time trying to keep the peace, avoiding uncomfortable conversations and convincing ourselves that staying quiet is somehow better for our relationships. But what if the very conversations we’re avoiding are the ones we need to be having?

We get into why avoiding conflict isn’t the same as keeping the peace, how our families shape the way we disagree, knowing which fights are worth having and how to navigate difficult conversations at work, at home and with the people we love. 

Learning how to disagree without losing our connection to each other is a skill. And it’s one I think ALL of us could get better at!!

Our episode is out now on @youtube, @applepodcasts, @spotify and wherever you get your podcasts 🎙️✨

At just 24, Nara has turned one of the most recognizable formats on the internet into a multimillion-dollar business, and she’s already thinking about what she wants to own and build next.

You’ll learn: ✨ How Nara turned viral videos into a real business ✨ Why she uses brand deals to test what her audience will actually buy ✨ How she and Lucky think about money and building wealth ✨ Why she still films and edits every video herself ✨ What the internet gets completely wrong about her ✨ Why social media is only the beginning

Every time I see a red carpet look that makes me stop scrolling, there’s a good chance @luxurylaw had something to do with it!!

I’ve admired Law’s work for years. His eye, his confidence, the way he’s helped create some of the most iconic fashion moments of our time. But what I admire just as much is the BUSINESS he’s built around that talent.

From growing up on the South Side of Chicago to becoming one of the most influential people in fashion, Law has never been afraid to know his worth, demand more for himself, and do things on his own terms.

And just when everyone thought he was at the top of his game, he decided to walk away!!! Now THAT is a conversation I wanted to have.

We get into his incredible partnership with Zendaya, why getting paid what you’re worth matters, the power of your reputation, and knowing when it’s time to write a completely new chapter.

Because I always say, being great at what you do is one thing. Knowing how to turn that greatness into a business is another!!

Law has SO much to teach us about both. This is such a good one!! Our episode is out now on @youtube, @applepodcasts, @spotify and wherever you listen!! 🎙️✨

posts.caption:
If you’ve been waiting for a sign from someone you’ve lost, you’re allowed to ask for one. 🤍

I ask for signs out loud all the time. Sometimes I get really specific and ask to see a blue butterfly, and other times I simply say, “I just need to know you’re here.”

When I sat down with @khloekardashian on the @khloeinwonderlandpod, she shared a story about her family that moved me so much. It’s a beautiful reminder that the connection with someone you love doesn’t end when they pass.

If there’s someone you’re missing today, comment their name below. I’ll hold them in my heart with you.

#signsfromtheuniverse #afterlife #kardashians #khloekardashian

Your nervous system responds to sound.
In this clip I share a simple humming technique that stimulates the vagus nerve and helps your body shift out of stress and into calm.

Click the link to get your free manifesting meditation.

The Universe works fast when you're having fun! Want to strengthen your faith in the Universe and Manifest Your Desires? Join me for my Trust The Universe Challenge 👆 

#theuniversehasyourback #positiveenergy #motivationaltalk #havemorefun

Surrender is the most powerful part of manifesting.

If you’ve been holding a desire so tightly that it feels heavy, this is your sign to loosen your grip. Your faith can stay strong while your hands stay open.

Save this for the next time you feel tempted to force it.

#manifesting #surrender #spiritualgrowth

You don't need to be in the room to receive the guidance. ✨

Livestream tickets for Dear Guides Live on 11/21 are now on sale. Tune in from wherever you are.

Comment DEARGUIDES for the link.

Dear Guides Live is where people come to unlock their psychic intuition and deepen their connection to angels and spirit guides by learning directly from world-renowned psychic mediums.

@maryannthemedium @radleighvalentine @mediumrebeccarosen @johnmedium 

#theuniversehasyourback

A change in direction doesn’t mean you’re off track.

Sometimes the detour is the guidance.

#spiritualguidance #faith #trusttheuniverse

I can’t tell you how many times my body said no and I talked myself right out of it. 🧘‍♀️

That’s why this practice from John hit me so hard. It’s so simple, and it gives you something real to measure that feeling against. 

Once you know what a yes feels like inside you, the no’s get so much louder. In people, in decisions, in everything. Your body is already giving you answers. I want you to start listening.

Save this for the next time you need to tell if it’s a yes or no.

Comment WATCH and I’ll send you the full episode with @psychicmediumje.

#spiritguides #trustyourself #innerknowing

✨ NEW: Dear Guides Live is officially available to livestream! ✨

If you can’t join us in NYC, you can now experience the entire event live from wherever you are. 🕊️

Your guides have been talking to you this whole time.

Every sign is a nudge from someone in your corner. The more you notice, the more they show up.

On November 21, I’m bringing four of the world’s most respected mediums to New York City for one day of live channeling, guided meditation, and learning to read your own signs. @maryannthemedium, @mediumrebeccarosen, @johnmedium and @radleighvalentine will be on stage with me at the SVA Theatre.

And now, you can join us in person OR via livestream.

Ready to finally hear them? Comment DEARGUIDES and I’ll send you all the details.

#spiritguides #psychicmedium #dearguides #liveworkshop

Surrender doesn’t mean you stop caring.

It means you stop trying to control every detail and let the Universe meet you halfway.

#surrender #lettinggo #trusttheuniverse

Your most creative self is already inside you. ✨

You don’t have to hustle your way into flow. Chaos and creation can’t share the same space, so when you slow down and quiet the noise, your true self comes forward.

That’s where your clearest ideas and boldest moves come from.

Thank you @codiesanchez for this conversation. Watch the full episode on @bigdeal.podcast.

#selfenergy #flowstate #creativity

Sometimes the biggest shift is becoming willing to believe something new. 🤍

The first word you see is what your heart is ready to believe in.

What did you get?

#faith #spiritualgrowth #selfbelief

John gave me a practice I’m doing tonight and you should too. 

You put a reminder in your calendar for one year from today and let your guides show you what’s coming. Don’t overthink it. If a red fire truck pops into your head, write down the red fire truck!

Then forget about it. I love the idea of my future self opening that note and going, wow, they really did know.

Comment WATCH and I’ll send you the full episode with @psychicmediumje.

#spiritguides #manifesting #intuition #intuition

linkedin.about:
Gary Vaynerchuk is a serial entrepreneur and serves as the Chairman of VaynerX, the CEO of VaynerMedia, and Creator and CEO of VeeFriends, and 6x New York Times Best Selling Author. Gary is considered one of the leading global minds on what's next in culture, business, and the internet.   

Known as "GaryVee," he is described as one of the most forward thinkers in business. He acutely recognizes trends and patterns early to help others understand how shifts in consumer attention impact the realities of the business world today. Gary's approach sits at the intersection of business and pop culture. He keenly understands how to bring brand relevance to the forefront. He is a prolific angel investor with early investments in companies like Facebook, Twitter, Tumblr, Venmo, Snapchat, Coinbase, and Uber.    

Gary is an entrepreneur at heart – he builds businesses. Today, he helps Fortune 1000 brands leverage consumer attention through his full-service advertising agency, VaynerMedia, which has ofﬁces in Amsterdam, Bangkok, Chicago, Delhi, Kuala Lumpur, London, Los Angeles, Mexico City, Miami, New York, Tokyo, Toronto, Singapore, and Sydney. VaynerMedia is part of the VaynerX modern-day parent company, which also includes Eva Nosidam Productions, Gallery Media Group, ChukMedia, VaynerSpeakers, VaynerCommerce, Tamara Group, and Tingley Lane Trading. Gary is the Co-Founder of VaynerSports, VCR Group, VaynerWatt, Resy, and Empathy Wines. He guided Resy and Empathy to successful exits -- which he later sold to American Express and Constellation Brands, respectively. He also owns a Major League Pickleball team called the 5s, is part owner of a Big3 basketball team, and is an investor in the revival of the SlamBall League.   

Gary is also the founder and creator of VeeCon – a contemporary super conference that converges business and pop culture with innovation and technology. In addition to running multiple businesses, Gary documents his daily life as a CEO through his social media channels, which have more than 50 million followers and garner more than 2+ billion impressions per year across all platforms. His podcast, "The GaryVee Audio Experience," ranks among the top podcasts globally.    

Gary serves on the board of MikMak, Bojangles Restaurants, Global Citizen Forum, The Paley Center, and Pencils of Promise. He is also an advisor for District and a longtime Well Member of charity: water.  

Gary's life ambition is to buy the New York Jets.

posts.caption:
Flew to New York as the only creator representing India at LinkedIn’s Connection by Design, hosted at their office inside the Empire State Building.

Here’s what LinkedIn showed us:

• Business Cards: create a digital card, save it to your phone wallet and turn an IRL conversation into a lasting connection. We got an early preview, with a global rollout planned by the end of October.
• Creator Dashboard: audience growth, post performance and insights into who you’re reaching.
• Content management: published posts, drafts and scheduled posts together in the dashboard.
• Pinned comments are back, so you can highlight useful information and conversations.
• Creator Marketplace: opt in so brands can discover you through your content and audience, opening up potential paid partnerships.
• In-Stream Video Ads: a new monetisation opportunity being tested with selected creators and advertisers.
• Advice Sessions: offer paid 1:1 sessions, set your price and let people book directly from your profile. Available to US Premium Business subscribers.
• Prospect Suggestions: discover relevant potential clients and collaborators.
• Private connection notes: remember where you met someone and pick up the conversation later.
• Multiple roles: show the companies behind your different current roles at the top of your profile.

Some of the earning tools are still early-access or invite-only.

The biggest takeaway from the panels: trust comes from showing up consistently, sharing your experience and building relationships before you need something.

Casey shared how one LinkedIn connection helped him go from selling artwork for around $500 to $10,000 pieces. A reminder that your next opportunity might start with one conversation.

Also got a headshot I love and tried BNTO’s colour analysis. Apparently, I’m a Dark Autumn.

Thank you, LinkedIn, for hosting me. Which update would you use first?

EXCLUSIVE: Leave a “YES” below and I’ll DM you my FULL episode with Two-time Paralympic gold medalist @ezrafrech👇

Ezra is only 21, but the way he thinks about confidence, pressure, failure, and purpose completely changed the way I see all four. Born with a limb difference, he grew up being stared at, underestimated, and told—sometimes with good intentions—that he didn’t have to expect as much from himself. Instead, he decided to expect more.

We talk about learning to fully accept his body, the painful moments that shaped his confidence, turning failure into motivation, becoming a Paralympic champion, competing on Dancing With the Stars, and why he believes confidence is built by keeping the promises you make to yourself.

But what inspires me most about Ezra isn’t what he’s overcome. It’s what he’s trying to change. He wants kids with disabilities to grow up seeing possibility instead of limitation—and he’s using sport, representation, and every platform he earns to help make that happen.

If you’ve ever been underestimated, struggled to accept a part of yourself, been afraid to dream bigger, or needed a reminder that you are capable of far more than other people may expect of you… this conversation is for you.

posts.caption:
Two years ago, I probably couldn’t have picked a dahlia out of a lineup, and here I am digging up an entire field of them. 😂

Some might think digging them up is sad, but I think it’s incredible to see the roots that were growing underneath it all. Everyone focuses on the flowers, but have you ever looked at a tuber? Isn’t it wild that flowers can grow out of a little lump that looks like a potato?

My fairy garden mother, @thefloweringfarmhouse, flew in to help me close out my first season as a dahlia micro farmer (yes, I’m claiming the title)!

Swipe through the whole process with us: cutting the still blooming field down, digging every clump up, washing off the dirt, and cutting the tubers apart, which is where we found that what I planted had easily tripled while I was busy admiring the blooms. 💐 

My life has forever changed from all the time spent with my hands in the soil. My brain is so full, but my heart is even fuller, and I’m fully and wildly in awe of the way nature and its cycles work.

Jen, thank you for flying in and for making me feel like I know what I’m doing out there. I kind of do now?! 🥰

posts.caption:
I waited seven years for an empty house. 🙃 Then we gave it back. 

For seven years, everything you’ve watched me build got made with a little one down the hall or heck, in my lap. 

So last year, when both girls went to full-day school, it felt like graduation. Honestly, kind of like retirement. Drew and I kept asking each other, what are we going to invent with all this time?

Confession: I didn’t rest in it. I sprawled out on the couch with the dogs, laptop on my knees, and filled every open hour with more work, because I could. 

Then one night at the end of summer, lying across the bed from Drew, I tossed out a question like it was nothing. His answer caught me so off guard that it changed our whole year.

The other morning it was 9:30, the girls were still in their pajamas, there were pancakes going, and my four-year-old said, We don’t have to rush out the door anymore.

I wrote the whole story down, the heart of it and the hard parts I don’t usually post about. (Head lice made the pros list. A class hamster named Pickles made the cons.)

If you’ve ever finally gotten the thing you were waiting for and realized it didn’t fit anymore, this one’s for you.

➡️ Comment: READ and I’ll send it straight to your DMs.
Photos by @angelarosegonzalez

posts.caption:
From a patch of grass to a full-fledged dahlia field, and somewhere along the way, a little more of me came up out of the ground too. 🌸

Thank you for not unfollowing when this account wandered from Pinterest tips to soil tests and yellowing leaves, because this little corner of the internet is for the whole human, not just one part of me, and this year a lot of me was out in the dahlias.

What started as a family project became how we connect with our community and with the earth, and I spent the season as a happy, curious student, getting so much of it wrong (so, so much) and wandering back out the next morning anyway, like the flowers might forgive me if I just kept showing up.

If you’ve ever stood in the middle of a perfectly fine life and wondered whether this is all there is, let me tell you from here in the dirt (on a screen, I know, I see the irony) that there’s so much more, and most of it is waiting somewhere your phone isn’t. Be a beginner at whatever makes you curious and put your hands on something alive. 

My urge to you is to let your work become the least interesting part of your life, it’s quite literally the best goal I’ve ever set. And if these garden posts nudged you to plant something, anything, tell me what, I want to cheer you on.

That’s a wrap on this growing season, the best adventure of our year, and I can’t wait to see what we do next year. 🥺

posts.caption:
You only get two things in this life 🤍

Moments. And relationships.

You can make the most of a moment, or you can ruin it by focusing on everything that’s unfair and everything you’re not getting.

We don’t get to choose the family we’re born into. But we do get to choose how we mend, build, and pour into every relationship we have. From someone you only get to say hi to for a few seconds, to my wife and my kids.

So many people are scared of wasting their life going after a dream that might not come true. That’s not the point. Make the most of the moments while you chase your goals with the people you love. When you do that, you win. Even if you lose.

posts.caption:
Imagine getting rejected from Shark Tank…before you even make it on the show. 😳

That's what happened to Barbara Corcoran. And what she did next? SO GOOD.

I love this story because it's a powerful reminder of how much rejection is part of the game when you're going after something big.

You're gonna hear NO. Sometimes a LOT.
The question is, what are you gonna do about it?

If you've been letting someone else's opinion stop you from going after what you want, take a page from Barbara's playbook. 💪

🎬 Comment INSIDER and I'll send you the full episode in your DMs.

October, you've been a busy one! 🍁

Here's a little behind-the-scenes peek at what I've been up to lately. Outdoor adventures, quality time with some of my favorite humans, and a whole lotta gratitude for this beautiful season.

How's October treating you? ❤️

This week on @prettytough, I’m joined by New York Times bestselling author @marieforleo. Coaching is one of my favorite subjects to cover with many of my guests and Marie has spent her career covering this field. 
We speak about building a career on your own terms, embracing reinvention, and trusting your gut in life’s biggest transitions. 💼💡⏱️ You can find the episode wherever you get your podcasts!

Just because you've been carrying something for years doesn't mean you have to keep lugging it around.

Especially if it's weighing you down. Maybe it's an old belief about who you're supposed to be. Or a responsibility you took on ages ago that no longer makes sense for your life.Whatever it is, here's something worth remembering:

You get to change your mind. You get to decide what's worth your time and energy NOW, even if you've spent years doing things differently.

And sometimes? Putting something down is exactly what you need to do to move forward. ❤️

I'm curious. What's something you're ready to let go of?

You don’t have to have it all figured out to be proud of yourself. 💛

You’re allowed to celebrate the version of you who’s still learning, growing, changing, and figuring it out as you go.

Give yourself some credit today. You’re doing better than you think. ✨

What’s something you’re proud of yourself for navigating lately? 👇

Rewinding to this conversation with Anastasia Soare, founder of Anastasia Beverly Hills. 💄

And WOW, did this part stick with me.

For years, Anastasia wished her straight hair were curly. Her hazel eyes were blue. She spent precious time wishing she could be someone else.

Sound familiar?

Then she learned to stop dimming herself and start owning exactly who she is.

Her words say it all:
“I never let anyone take my shine away, never ever. And you are unique, beautiful, and powerful.”

YES. 👏 Because your job isn’t to become someone else.
It’s to become more YOU.

Want the full conversation? Comment SHINE and I’ll send you the episode. 👇

Perfectionism can feel like you’re being thorough.

But sometimes, it’s just keeping you stuck. 😬

You don’t need every detail figured out before you take the next step. You need to be willing to start, learn, adjust, and keep moving.

Done doesn’t mean you stop caring. It means you stop waiting for perfect. ✨

What’s something you’ve been waiting to make “perfect” before you put it out into the world? 👇

Last year in Sicily 🍋, a villa owner told me something I still think about: “I don’t hire professionals.” 

The place was gorgeous. The food, the linens, the views… beyond.

But the PEOPLE were the magic. ✨

They were funny. Warm. Present. Kind. Playful. Nothing about it felt forced.

Especially Dora, the resident nonna and head chef. (That's us in the pic 💛 ) 

I spent as much time as I could in her kitchen, and when I left she gave me the biggest hug AND a big ol’ slap on the butt — just like my Grandma Mary used to. 😂😭

I asked the owner how he built a team like that. “I hire regular people who believe in making others feel welcome.”

That’s the part I can’t stop thinking about.

Because people can feel when there’s a real human on the other side. ❤️

And right now, when it’s easier than ever to crank out polished, perfectly acceptable words with AI, that human feeling matters even more.

Your stories. Your humor. Your weird little details. Your way of saying things.

That’s what makes people stop and feel something.

And yes — that’s ALSO what makes them buy. 💰

The Copy Cure teaches you how to write copy that sounds unmistakably like YOU and sells like hotcakes.

And for the first time EVER, it's $1000 off through October 16th.

Comment COPY and I’ll send you the details. 💌

Rewinding to my conversation with Simon Sinek. ✨

What if giving up was actually the thing that helped you find your way forward?

In my conversation with Simon Sinek, he shared a powerful story about the moment he stopped fighting so hard for a particular outcome—and what happened when he finally surrendered.

Sometimes, letting go doesn’t mean you’re giving up on your life or your dreams.

Sometimes, it means making space for what comes next. ✨

Want to hear Simon’s full story? Comment SURRENDER and I’ll send you the episode. 👇

Some words stick with you.

Over the years, I’ve collected a few quotes that genuinely changed the way I think, work, and move through life. 💭

These are a few I still come back to, because sometimes the right words at the right time can change everything.

Swipe through, and tell me: which one do you need to hear right now? 👇

Sometimes the voice telling you to quit is wisdom. Sometimes it’s fear, doubt, exhaustion, or the discomfort of doing something that actually matters. 💭

The trick is learning to tell the difference.

Before you give up, pause. Get curious. Ask yourself what’s really going on—and what you actually want.

What's something you quit that turned out to be a blessing? Tell me in the comments. 👇

Throwing it back to my conversation with Lewis Howes. 

There’s a big difference between easy money and making money easy. 💰

In my conversation with Lewis Howes, we talked about the temptation to chase the shortcut—the next big opportunity, the get-rich-quick promise, the thing that looks like easy money.

But “easy money” can come with a very expensive lesson.

Making money easy is different. It’s about building the skills, experience, and systems that make creating wealth more sustainable over time.

Want to hear the full conversation with Lewis? Comment MONEY and I’ll send you the episode. 👇

posts.caption:
My husband @the.chrisrobbins took me hiking for my birthday, and I learned something I will never forget…

Chris loves hiking. He’s experienced, he’s fast, and I’m usually somewhere behind him wondering if I’m slowing him down. 

But then he shared something a monk once taught him…

With every step you take, imagine you’re giving the earth a little massage 🌎

Instead of rushing to get somewhere, slow down. Feel the ground beneath your feet. Be present. Imagine that every step is bringing a little peace and positive energy into the world.

I had NEVER thought about walking that way before, suddenly, it wasn’t about how fast I could hike or how far we could go.

It was about being here. Together. Surrounded by all this beauty.
What a beautiful reminder that you don’t always need to get somewhere to enjoy where you are.

Sometimes the best thing you can do is slow down and enjoy every step ❤️
posts.alt: Video by Mel Robbins on October 18, 2026. May be an image of smiling and text.

posts.caption:
I was SO frustrated the other day. 

You know that feeling when you want to fix everything right now? I’ve learned that those are the moments when I need to get active, not reactive.

Literally.

I stop what I’m doing, get outside, and MOVE. Not to ignore the problem, but to give myself a chance to let go of that negative energy before I do something I’ll regret.

Going for a walk isn’t going to solve the issue at hand or make all my problems go away, but it does help me deal with them with a clearer mind.

Because here’s the thing… you can feel frustrated without letting the frustration control you.

Your power is in how you respond.

And sometimes, all it takes is a good walk to find that power again.

posts.caption:
The magic happens when you stop trying to get it perfect and trust what you already know.

I love this quote from American saxophonist, Charlie “Bird” Parker.

It’s all about the power of preparation.

You practice. You study. You put in the reps. You learn your craft so well that when it’s time, you can stop obsessing about getting it “right” and trust yourself.

Because preparation isn’t supposed to make you rigid. It’s supposed to make you free.

Do the work. Learn your instrument. Then when it’s your turn, stop overthinking and just wail. ❤️

Want a smoothie recipe for glowing skin? 

Try this one from Mayo Clinic dermatologist Dr. Saranya Wyles (@drwyles.derm)!

Comment “SKIN” and I’ll DM you the full episode.

Smoothie Recipe:

Ingredients
- 3-4 medium apples (Gala, Fuji or Pink Lady)
- 3-4 medium beets
- 3-4 large carrots
- 1 cup water (or minimum required by pressure cooker)
- 1/4 teaspoon ground turmeric (optional)
- 1-2 tbsp Flax seeds and chia seeds
- Coconut water
- Optional: protein powder

Directions
1. Cook the apples, beets, and carrots in an Instant Pot or slow cooker until soft. Store for easy prep.
2. Add a scoop of the cooked mixture to a blender with the seeds and turmeric.
3. Pour in coconut water to your desired consistency, add optional protein, and blend until smooth!

Hear more from Dr. Wyles on this episode of @themelrobbinspodcast to learn what foods support skin health from the inside out.

This episode will completely change how you think about your skin health!

What would you let an AI agent buy without asking you first?

Coming soon.

Everyone in China says ‘ecosystem, ecosystem, ecosystem.’ Foundery is a small attempt at trying to build that for consumer brands in India. It’s not about how many of the 20 brands per batch succeed or what valuations they achieve, but about the fact that, in 10 years, we would have built the rails and the ‘ecosystem’ by attempting to create 200 Indian brands with the potential to sell globally..

@jointhefoundery

Korea exported culture. 
Then the world bought Korean…

India has Bollywood, music, food, fashion, yoga and Ayurveda, a cultural moat very few countries can replicate..
Maybe we need to stop thinking only about exporting products and start deliberately exporting India. 
Consumer brands could follow.

The test of a first-rate intelligence is the ability to hold two opposed ideas in the mind at the same time, and still retain the ability to function.” — F. Scott Fitzgerald

The internet increasingly rewards the angrier, louder side, the more certain-sounding side, often the stupider side.

Maybe intelligence is being able to understand why the other side believes what it believes.

Introducing WTF: Discourse.

Two opposing ideas. Two people who actually believe them. No winner. Just the strongest version of both arguments.

You decide what you believe.
Did a travel episode, lots of insights and opportunities in this, basic premise was how to get the no of foreign visitors in India to go up from 10 million, but also what to build, live now

India gets about 10 million foreign tourists a year.

Dubai gets 18 million.

Dubai is basically one long road. We are 1.4 billion people with the Himalayas, Goa, Rajasthan, Kerala, the Andamans, 5,000 years of history and arguably the best food in the world :)

Something doesn’t add up.

Two men who built India’s biggest travel and hotel businesses agree on one thing: the country is easy to leave, hard to visit.

India has transformed dramatically over the last decade, better roads, airports, digital infrastructure and connectivity. Maybe tourism is the next big opportunity.

In this episode, the CEOs of MakeMyTrip and IHCL (Taj Hotels) tell us 5 things that could get a lot more of the world to come visit India, and where the opportunities for entrepreneurs might lie along the way.

Episode out now..

WTF Offline.

1 stadium. 10 hours. 150 people

No cameras, no press, no phones.

No audience either. Just friends and people I have had on the podcast over the years.

A safe space for conversations to happen differently when there’s no camera to perform for.

PS: We capped it at 150 people, partly to keep it intimate and partly because 151 onwards it starts to sound like the beginning of a cult :)

Travel inwards can bring in forex, jobs, and a lot of growth: a little more budget allocation, a slight tweak in attitude, a realisation that atithi devo bhava is better practiced than recited, like most other things in life. We all touch MakeMyTrip and Taj Hotels as Indians at some point. The two of them break down business opportunities and 5 things that need to change structurally.

Coming soon..

Big dreams demand more than just ambition. They demand sacrifices, uncomfortable decisions, sleepless nights, and the willingness to keep going when nobody understands why you’re doing what you’re doing.

There will be days when your goal is all you can think about, when you have to choose between what feels good today and what could change your life tomorrow. You’ll have to invest your time, energy, money, and attention long before you see any results.

And that’s the part people don’t talk about enough. Everyone wants the outcome, but not everyone is willing to pay the price it takes to get there.

The bigger the dream, the greater the responsibility you have to yourself to show up for it.

Just make sure that while you’re building the life you want, you don’t lose sight of the life you’re living.
Tomorrow 9:09 PM

One of the biggest mistakes you can make is spending your energy trying to change someone’s opinion of you.

You work harder, achieve more, explain yourself, and keep looking for that one moment when they finally acknowledge your worth. But the truth is, some people will never see you differently, no matter how much you accomplish.

And the longer you chase their validation, the more time you take away from building the life you actually want.

Not everyone needs to understand your journey. Not everyone needs to believe in your potential. And not everyone deserves a front-row seat to your progress.

Your potential is too valuable to be wasted on proving people wrong.

Focus on becoming the person you want to be. Let your growth be for yourself, not a performance for people who have already made up their minds.

The goal isn’t to make everyone believe in you. It’s to reach a point where you no longer need them to.

linkedin.about:
Randi Zuckerberg has long been a pioneer in both technology & media. As an early employee at Facebook & the creator of Facebook Live, she was on the front lines of shaping the social internet & how billions interact with content. Her lifelong passion for the arts paired with her tech career has been pivotal in her quest to help families navigate the complexities of an increasingly digital landscape.

Now, her unique skillset is more valuable than ever as these worlds collide with the emergence of AI & blockchain. As both an early adopter & prominent voice for women in crypto-adoption, Randi knows firsthand that these disruptive technologies offer unparalleled opportunities for autonomy, ownership, & financial success to creators and consumers alike. 

In response to the crypto market’s growing gap in diversity, inclusion, & accessibility, Randi founded HUG in early 2022 with the mission of empowering artists to become successful creative entrepreneurs. HUG is an inclusive social platform that democratizes access to the arts by providing creators with tooling to showcase & sell both physical & digital work, while also connecting them with one another & one-of-a-kind opportunities for their art.

As of 2024, Randi’s leadership has led HUG to become a global community of more than 35,000 artists from 170 countries & counting, with Randi having personally mentored over a thousand of them with their crypto-enabled businesses. HUG continues to support artists through its three core tenets of discovery, opportunity, & education, & has to date placed thousands of independent artists into their first exhibitions around the world. HUG has also distributed over $300,000 in grants & scholarships directly to independent creators, & continues to partner with entities such as L'Oréal, Mastercard, Forbes, Christie's, MoMA, the United Nations, & more in support of artists & creative technologists. 

Randi holds a Bachelor of Arts in Psychology from Harvard University. She serves as both an investor & advisor to several early & mid-stage companies and sits on the board of directors for The Motley Fool & Life360.

Alongside her career as a tech innovator, she is an accomplished artist & producer who has performed on Broadway, winning three Tony awards. She hosts a weekly business talk radio show, Randi Zuckerberg Means Business, on SiriusXM. She is an avid runner, having completed several ultra-marathons with podium finishes. While she may be known as “Mom to Start-ups”, Randi spends her days learning, growing, & sharing her love for arts with her husband and children.

posts.caption:
✨🦄 NEW PR AT THE BOSTON MARATHON!!! 🦄✨

3:27:37
7:55/mile pace
Four minute PR from my best previous time at Berlin 2024

Honestly, still speechless over this. I cannot believe that at age 44, one week after a 100k race, five months post-injury…that this happened. An entire marathon at a mile pace that starts with a 7! A Boston Qualifying time AT BOSTON! And to do this with my son here with me! OMFG!!! 

Have been working so so hard, and it doesn’t always come together on race day. But when it does…there’s no feeling quite like it. 

Time to go eat all the food and cry so many happy tears.

Fastest Known Time on the Baja Sur 135km Trail! 

On March 6, I attempted the Fastest Known Time (FKT) for Mexico’s 135km Baja Sur Trail across the entire Baja Sur Peninsula. 

82 miles from the Pacific Ocean → Sea of Cortez.
13,000 feet of elevation.
One absolutely savage mountain section from miles 17–34 that climbed 6,000 feet in just 6 miles — including three straight miles at 30% grade in peak heat.
40 miles through night under the moon and stars.
One 5-minute dirt nap after mile 60.
And a sunrise at mile 70 that made the entire effort feel almost spiritual.

My first “comeback” ultra distance after injury. 

Final result?
24 hours, 53 minutes, 10 seconds

Which was the Fastest Known Time for ANYONE on that trail, male or female

FKTs are different than races.
There are no set aid stations.
No course marshals or race directors. 
You build the entire attempt yourself — the logistics, the pacing plan, the fueling, the documentation — and then you go see if your body and mind can execute it.

This one took an incredible team.
Huge gratitude to my pacers — including my ride or die @dr.joelipsky, absolute rock star running partner Ben Thompson, and the incredible @joecorcione who agreed to run 60+ miles of the effort with me, including the insane mountain climb section, on just a few days of notice. These incredible friends rotated through the desert with me for nearly 25 straight hours, alongside a support vehicle leapfrogging us for lightning-fast resupplies.

The mountain was the hardest trail I’ve ever climbed.
But running under the stars, seeing the desert sunrise, laughing through the pain cave and finishing on the beach after running across an entire peninsula?

That’s a feeling I’ll carry for a long time.

Lots more to come including more incredible footage, but wanted to share as soon as we completed the attempt successfully. Thank you to Ben and the Joes 😂 Thank you to @linsanityz @mounttocoast (should be renamed coast to mount to coast?) Thank you to the amazing @drmeganroche who saved my quads and my fueling strategy. Thanks to @jhenwood72 for leaning into the crazy with me. And thank you to all my friends and family cheering me on from afar.

Same genes, same outfits, same inability to have any chill whatsoever. Laughed the entire way home. Pure joy, silliness, endorphins, and memories.

My ginormous baby is TWELVE today!!! 🥹🎂❤️

We are celebrating with a mother-son adventure in Chicago! A weekend of running, matching outfits, deep dish pizza, friends and birthday surprises. 

Happy birthday, Simi! I love watching you grow up, even if I wish you’d slow down just a tiny bit. (Vertically and literally)

We are officially an entire running family now. 

Today’s family scoreboard at the Run For Love 5k:

🏆 Asher WON THE ENTIRE RACE! 

🔥 Shira broke 10 MINUTES in the mile!!! 
Tiny legs, enormous swagger.

🏃 Simi casually knocked out 5 miles BEFORE the 5k for an 8-mile long run as training for his half marathon

🥉 Mom took 3rd overall female in the 5K, desperately clinging to relevance as Asher smoked her

❤️ Dad paced Simi to glory for his entire 8 mile run and coached Shira with a last minute pep talk at the start line. 

PRs. Podiums. Long runs. Matching outfits. Donuts. 

I fear I have created exactly the monsters I intended to create.

Miami 100 mile ultra.
First place female and second fastest female time ever!

Miami, you were beautiful, painful, chaotic, insane and amazing in all the best ways. The race was an adventure-style checkpoint race, where you didn’t learn the course until you were in it, and you got the directions for each checkpoint in real time. I ran over bridges, around islands, through neighborhoods, and navigated crowded touristy areas. All in hot and crazy humid Florida weather. 

When @joecorcione said he thought I was capable of running a ~20 hour 100 miler time (roughly a 12 minute mile, including stops) I didn’t quite believe him. My PR for the distance is 23:30 which I just ran in July. 

But 20 hours and 24 minutes later, I crossed the finish line as first place female and third place overall, averaging a 12:03 pace after running 100 miles non-stop, with very few breaks, except to change water logged sneakers a few times or use the restroom.

But a race performance like this doesn’t happen without an absolute incredible crew firing on all cylinders. @murrclurr_ is beyond amazing as a crew chief. @joecorcione and Ben Thompson did an unreal job pacing, helping me navigate the course, and pushing me through peak heat. And my husband @btworetzky absolutely crushed it on my crew out there. This race was just as challenging to crew, as to run, and I was in absolute awe of my team the entire time. 

Special shoutout to @dr.joelipsky who wasn’t physically there with us, but absolutely was in spirit, and helped me crush one of the best training blocks I’ve ever had. And to @pinknoelephants who has become an essential part of the team and @quietgratefullife who surprised me out on the course. 

My legs are sore and my body is a bit wrecked, but my heart is so happy and I feel beyond proud and excited for what lies beyond.

The past few days have seen some fun milestones!!

🍊 My 1,000th OrangeTheory class! 
I walked into OTF almost four years ago with no clue how that gym would change my life. Countless 6am classes, some of my closest friendships, big goals dreamt & done, and a whole lot of life lived under those orange lights. Naturally, we celebrated the only reasonable way: a 6am toga party. 

🔥 My son’s new 5k PR! I got to run side by side in matching outfits with my son Simi, as he dug so deep and set a new PR on the exact same course where he last set a PR at this distance, two years ago. Super proud mom. Even prouder of the fact that Simi has poured so much heart into his Team for Kids charity fundraiser for his upcoming Disney race. 

🏙️ Bronx 10 Mile: My first ever 10 mile race! The course was so fun - starting and ending at Yankee Stadium. And my first time racing for @jhenwood72’s @henwoodshounds team. Held a 7:24/mile pace and felt so good doing it. Even better was getting to run bonus warm-up and cool down miles to and from the race with Sydney.

Three milestones that look totally different on paper. My first race for a new team. My kid’s PR. A hilariously large number of 6am workouts.

But really, they’re all the same thing. Keep showing up for yourself and find people who make showing up wildly fun. 

Oh. And always, always wear a costume.

Apparently tapering for a race doesn’t HAVE to be a disaster. (Who knew?)

This week included: 70 miles, an actual full rest day (!!) and a truly unreasonable amount of fun:

👫 Doubles HYROX with my husband — we crushed our goals and had an absolute blast. Thank goodness for his ability to pull a sled and let me passenger princess that one…

🏃‍♀️ A long run to visit a friend, because apparently I now make house calls by foot

🏃‍♂️ Intervals with rock star friend + pacer Ben, who for some reason, continues to voluntarily participate in my nonsense

😂 An “apology tour” park loop — because deep conversations are always better while moving your body

🔥 Live Peloton class with Matt Wilpers + some of my favorite Pelo-friends

💪 Another live Tread with Mariana Fernandez, side-by-side with my bestie Sydney — who is about to CRUSH her 70.3 Half Ironman!!!

🛋️ AN ACTUAL REST DAY. Please respect my privacy during this unprecedented time.

🍎🍯 A beautiful Rosh Hashanah run with my husband + 11-year-old son, who is 500 miles into his goal of running 800 miles this year for charity. Proud mom. 

🌧️ Urban Iron with my 15-year-old in the pouring rain: 8.6 miles, 3 gyms with strength workouts, a post-race cold plunge that didn’t even make us any wetter than we already were, and an obscene amount of energy beverages that we accidentally thought were recovery beverages.

🏁 Holding the finisher tape at the NYRR 5th Avenue Mile ❤️ This was such a cool life experience. 

And because I don’t want to falsely advertise emotional stability during taper week…

A formal apology to my mahjong friends, who witnessed the portion of the taper where I VERY MUCH did not hold it together.

Turns out ugly crying and mahjong are, in fact, compatible activities. 😂🀄️

93 miles this week in the most unhinged, fun, “Randi” way ever

🏃‍♀️ Monday: A new 50K PR in a time trial with @dr.joelipsky biking alongside me for all 31.1 miles
🌙 Thursday (Weds night?): An all-out 1-mile race through Times Square at 1AM with my son 
@orchardstreetrunners absolutely epic OSR1
🎥: Also Thursday: Live taping of a Peloton tread class with @mattwilpers 
💪 Friday: A solo HYROX with @sydneysmith812 — and my husband cheering. And then getting to cheer for him! 
🏅 Sunday: Carderock Trail Half Marathon in 1:45:43 — 4th place woman, 1st in my age group!
Thanks @bishopseventsllc for the awesome event!

Plus so many shared fun social miles and workouts in between with some of my favorite people. 

On paper, 93 miles sounds like a pretty solitary pursuit. But even though it was tough and my body feels a bit wrecked, none of my favorite miles this week felt solo.

They looked like an incredible friend and coach pedaling beside me for hours. My son, who has become one of my favorite running partners, lining up with me at 1AM, laughing about how fun and crazy we are. A best friend willingly following me to DC to join my latest terrible idea. An amazing coach in @joecorcione encouraging me to push to new levels. And a husband who has apparently accepted that “what are we doing this weekend?” is now a dangerous question that includes destroying our bodies and eating a LOT of delicious carbs. 

I’m proud of the miles and grateful for a body that carried me through my biggest training week ever.

But mostly, I’m grateful for the people, the adventures, and the memories. 

And now, for my hardest endurance event of all: sitting down.

Thanks to @dhash for the incredible pics from OSR1

Normal mother-son activities: dinner, movies, a board game

Us: racing one mile at 1am through Times Square 🏃‍♀️🏃‍♂️

Do I have a mini me or what?! 😂 

Some families make memories during normal waking hours. We are not those families. 

Thanks @orchardstreetrunners for the awesome vibes and great memories. 

Side note: Both Asher and I got PRs in the mile! Asher ran a 5:05 and I ran a 6:24!

In a ​2008 paper​ published in the Journal of Experimental Social Psychology, researchers at the University of Virginia sought to study the impact of social support on how we perceive challenges.

In the first study, the researchers had a group of participants stand at the base of a steep 26° hill wearing a heavy backpack. Some of the participants were alone, while others were paired with a friend. Then they asked the participants to estimate the hill’s steepness.

The findings were fascinating:

Participants who were paired with a friend estimated the hill to be significantly less steep than those who were alone.

Relationship duration with the friend correlated negatively with perceived steepness. The longer the friendship, the gentler the hill appeared.

In a follow-up study, the researchers had the participants stand alone and simply imagine either a supportive person (friend), neutral person (store clerk), or negative person (someone who had betrayed them).

Once again, the results were clear:

Participants who imagined a supportive person saw the hill as less steep than those who imagined neutral or negative people.

The closeness and warmth of the imagined relationship were negatively correlated with perceived steepness. The better the relationship, the gentler the hill appeared.

The researchers concluded that the brain treats supportive relationships as a psychological energy resource. When you feel connected, your brain effectively lightens the load.

The challenge doesn’t change, but the perception of that challenge does.

Because challenges and struggles are inevitable.

But facing them alone is optional.
