What do you say to your family when you don’t know if you’ll ever see them again?

In February 2022, he told his wife and children the war had begun. Then he left as Russian forces advanced towards Kyiv, unsure what the coming hours would bring.

This is President Volodymyr Zelenskyy (zelenskyy_official) 

Before politics, he built a successful career in Ukrainian television as a writer, producer and performer, even portraying a president on screen. In 2019, he was elected President of Ukraine. Three years later, Russia launched its full-scale invasion.

Sitting down with him was surreal and an enormous responsibility. It was a rare chance to hear his account of the first hours of the war and the decisions that followed.

We discussed things like:

- How he found out Russia had invaded.
- Why he refused an offer to evacuate Kyiv.
- The 64km Russian military convoy advancing towards the capital.
- How Russian forces tried to capture a key airport.
- His account of discovering hundreds of bodies after Russian occupation.
- What he believes it will take to end the war.

But I also wanted to understand how he’d been coping.

One of my first questions was simply, “How are you doing?” His answer was: “It’s hard.”

He spoke about meeting parents whose children had been killed. Some, he explained, simply ask him for a hug.

And as he spoke, there were tears in his eyes.

Whatever your views on the war or the decisions made by those involved, this is a rare opportunity to hear his account of events that have changed millions of lives.

Because behind every map, every headline and every political decision, there are real people.

Out now on all platforms ❤️👊🏾

(President Zelenskyy was recorded in Ukrainian and dubbed in English.)

My nigerian mum raised 4 of us without being able to read or write herself, having left school when she was a child in Nigeria.

I struggled with school too - I wasn’t a smart kid and couldn’t pay attention, so I quickly realised the “traditional path” wasn’t going to work for someone like me

Then, when I was 12 years old, I discovered Dragons’ Den! 🐉

Me and my mum both fell in love with the show. Looking back, I think entrepreneurship offered us both hope - a path to a better life for people like us, who couldn’t pass tests in a classroom but were willing to work hard.

At 12 I would pause the TV and give my verdict, as if I was the 6th Dragon

By 16 I’d discovered Shark Tank and was starting my first (terrible) businesses

By 18 I was a university dropout with a start-up

And somehow, 9 years later, I ended up sitting in one of those Dragons’ Den chairs I used to shout at from our sofa

My mum has never fully gotten over it. 

When I call her today, 6 years later, the conversation is still 80% Dragons’ Den - her opinion on what I said, the businesses, what SHE would have done...

Btw, i’m genuinely not sure if she knows I have a podcast 😂 i don’t think she’s ever mentioned it 😅

But she knows Dragons’ Den, and that’s more than enough for her.

I know she’s always wanted me to do Shark Tank, so this phone call - telling her that day had come absolutely made my day, and hopefully her’s too!

I very much hope to do her proud + all of you that have supported me for the longest time... wish me luck!! 👊🏾❤️

P.S who would win in a fight, a shark 🦈 or a dragon 🐉 ???

Can someone who’s never coded, but has the best vibe coding tools, beat an engineer using the old methods?

It intrigues me how much kids learn simply by observing their parents and elders around them: what we speak, what we do, our words, and our actions.

A couple of weeks back, there was a very special occasion when we were introducing our elder kid to the world of triathlons. I was walking to the venue when I asked him whether he knew what he had to do. I was expecting him to say that he would have to swim, cycle, and run, and his answer literally stopped me in my tracks. 

He said, “Finish.”

This is exactly the answer I would have given if somebody asked me this question. There is a lot of glory in competing, but there is an incredible amount of character building in just completing what you’ve started.

Sometimes I wonder if he’s been listening in on some of the calls and meetings at home and work over the last 6 months. We have been speaking to so many of our colleagues and our investors about holding tight when the going gets tough and finishing what we started. Who knows? I’m not sure, but I know that if this kid remembers this little lesson in life - that completing matters as much, if not more, than competing - he sure is going to go a long way in life.

🫶🫶🫶

p.s. Also, every time I see this reel, it absolutely cracks me up how both mother and son decided to jump into the pool while holding their noses 😂
